perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s perspective, the available information is:

- I am Harold Padilla, a project manager. Arthur Begum is a police officer and a friend I often rely on for advice.
- I felt frustrated and anxious because I believed my project team was unmotivated and our progress was suffering.
- I arranged and attended a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur and told him I was at my wit’s end.
- Arthur told me motivation can be tricky; I should try to understand what drives each team member individually; people need to feel valued and understood; and I should have one-on-one conversations with them.
- I felt hopeful and relieved, believed Arthur’s advice could help, and decided to implement it.
- In a team meeting, I proposed quick one-on-one chats to learn what motivates each person. I heard one team member say it could be helpful and another say they were open to it. I said I would schedule time with each of them and urged us to make the project a success together.
- Later, I noticed the team still was not responding well. I felt disappointed and worried and told Arthur so.
- Arthur told me there might be deeper issues: personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors. He suggested I might need to dig deeper. I decided to set up another round of meetings.
- In one-on-one meetings, I asked team members about concerns. I heard that there was tension between a few team members affecting work, and that another team member felt overwhelmed by the workload and struggled to stay motivated under constant stress.
- I said I would look into resolving conflicts and see about redistributing tasks to ease pressure, and that their well-being was important to me.
- I felt optimistic and empowered. I planned regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive and open team environment.
- I told the team about these changes. I heard one team member say it sounded great and would help us work better together, and another agree that it was good their concerns were being addressed. I said we would work together to make the project a success and that their input and well-being were crucial.
